turns.content:
## Retries (taskq 4.x)
Declare retry behaviour on the task decorator:

    @queue.task(max_retries=3, backoff='exponential', backoff_base=2.0, backoff_max=600)
    def send_invoice(invoice_id): ...

- max_retries: number of retries after the first attempt (default 0).
- backoff: 'fixed' | 'linear' | 'exponential'. Delay for attempt n is backoff_base ** n seconds, capped at backoff_max.
- jitter: bool, default True. Adds up to 25% random delay.

## Non-retryable errors
Raise taskq.Abort to fail a job permanently without consuming retries. Alternatively pass no_retry_for=(ExcType, ...) to the decorator; exceptions of these types mark the job as failed immediately.

## Changed in 4.0
The retry_on= argument from 3.x was removed. Use no_retry_for= (deny-list) instead of retry_on= (allow-list).

## Dead letter queue
Jobs that exhaust retries are moved to the queue named '<queue>.dead' when dead_letter=True is set on the Queue.

The portal holds names, addresses, order history and partial card details for approximately 48,000 customers.

Finding 2 (high). The office network is a single flat segment. Printers, the door-access controller, guest wifi devices and the finance team's workstations can all reach each other directly. From a guest wifi connection the tester was able to reach the administrative interface of the door controller, which still used the manufacturer's default password.

Finding 3 (high). Backups of the main file server are written nightly to a network share on the same domain, using an account that is also a domain administrator. An attacker who compromised that account could delete or encrypt both the live data and the backups. No offline or immutable copy exists. The last documented restore test was 26 months ago.

Finding 4 (medium). Of 85 staff who received the simulated phishing email, 23 clicked the link and 11 entered their password on the fake page. Multi-factor authentication is enabled for email but not for the VPN or the finance system.

Finding 5 (medium). Fourteen of the 30 laptops sampled were more than 90 days behind on operating system updates. Disk encryption was enabled on all of them.

Finding 6 (low). The public website discloses its exact software version in response headers. The version in use is current.

Positive observations. Disk encryption coverage is complete. Email filtering blocked two of the three test attachments. Staff reported the phishing email to IT within 14 minutes of it being sent, although the report was not acted on for a further three hours.

The assessors consider findings 1 and 3 together to represent the greatest risk to the business: the first exposes customer data directly, and the second means a ransomware incident could be unrecoverable.

Give me a neutral 100-word summary of this press piece and then a list of the claims that are unverified or come only from the company.

LINDENVALE — Regional delivery company Swiftparcel announced on Monday that it will replace a quarter of its van fleet with electric cargo bikes in the city's inner suburbs by the middle of next year, in what it described as the largest such rollout in the country.

The company, which employs about 600 people and handles an estimated 40,000 parcels a day, said 120 bikes would operate from three new 'micro-depots' in converted car parks. Vans will bring parcels to the depots overnight and riders will complete the final leg. Swiftparcel's chief executive told reporters the change would cut the company's inner-city delivery emissions by 70 percent and make deliveries 'on average 15 minutes faster' because bikes can use lanes and laneways closed to vans.

The company said no drivers would lose their jobs and that existing staff would be offered retraining as riders or depot staff. A union representing delivery workers said it had not been consulted before the announcement and was seeking details on pay rates for riders, who it said are often engaged as contractors rather than employees elsewhere in the industry. 'We welcome fewer vans. We do not welcome fewer rights,' its secretary said.

A transport researcher at the city's university, who was not involved in the plan, said cargo bikes had been shown to work well in dense European centres but that results depended heavily on depot location and on the size of parcels. 'A bike is excellent for shoeboxes and poor for flat-pack furniture,' she said. She added that the speed claim was plausible in peak hours but that she had not seen the company's data.

The city council, which leases two of the three car parks to the company, said the arrangement was a twelve-month trial and that it would monitor footpath congestion and complaints. A local traders' group said it was worried about the loss of 46 public parking spaces.

Swiftparcel did not disclose the cost of the programme. It said the first depot would open in February.
